title: Installation Coverage of Automatic Reissues
content:
**Scope.** This schedule applies to SSL/TLS Certificates installed by Harborline support as a managed installation on a server outside Harborline hosting. It fixes how many certificates one managed installation covers. The managed installation charge applies the product's installation fee once for every certificate covered.

## 1. What a managed installation covers

A managed installation covers the certificate it installs. On the same server it also covers the automatic reissues of that certificate which the subscription's domain validation method lets Harborline install without the customer. The validation method recorded on the subscription decides which reissues those are:

| Validation method on the subscription | Certificates covered by one managed installation |
|---|---|
| DNS CNAME record | the certificate installed, plus every automatic reissue before the subscription end date |
| HTTP file (the validation file is already on the server) | the certificate installed, plus the automatic reissues issued on or before the date domain control was last validated plus the product's domain validation reuse period (200 days on every product) |
| approver email | only the one certificate installed |

## 2. The automatic reissue schedule used for counting

- An automatic reissue replaces the current certificate 30 days before that certificate expires.
- No automatic reissue replaces a certificate that expires on the subscription end date.
- A reissued certificate is valid for 200 days if it is issued before 15 March 2027, and for 100 days if it is issued on or after 15 March 2027. It never runs beyond the subscription end date.
- A reissue that is already due (its date is today or has passed) counts as issued today.

So a reissue issued on 14 March 2027 runs 200 days and one issued on 15 March 2027 runs 100 days, in both cases cut off at the subscription end date. For the HTTP file method, a reissue falling on the last day of the reuse period is covered. One falling on the following day is not.

## 3. Hypothetical illustration

All figures below are invented. Today is 4 May 2032. The current certificate expires on 19 June 2032 and the subscription ends on 2 August 2033.

- **Reissue dates.** On this schedule the automatic reissues fall on 20 May 2032, 29 July 2032, 7 October 2032, 16 December 2032, 24 February 2033 and 5 May 2033. The last of them expires on the subscription end date, so it is not replaced.
- **DNS CNAME record.** All six reissues are covered, so the installation covers seven certificates.
- **HTTP file, with domain control last validated on 15 March 2032.** The reuse period ends on 1 October 2032. The 20 May and 29 July reissues fall on or before that date, so the installation covers three certificates.
- **Approver email.** The installation covers one certificate.

A second hypothetical: today is 4 May 2032, the current certificate expired on 30 April 2032 and the subscription ends on 11 October 2032, with the DNS CNAME record method. The reissue that is already due counts as issued today and runs to 12 August 2032. The next reissue, on 13 July 2032, runs to the subscription end date. The installation therefore covers three certificates.
